Europe’s Modelled €5.70/kg Hydrogen Faces Industrial Buyers Who Can Afford Far Less

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (956 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, europe’s industrial hydrogen looks have a buyer problem.
  • In a recent development, the central 2050 scenario in my European hydrogen assessment puts on-site production at €5.70/kg.
  • At a factory using hydrogen for process heat, €5.70/kg is an expensive fuel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, europe’s industrial hydrogen looks have a buyer problem. A factory cannot make its products competitive by paying whatever a new hydrogen plant needs to recover its investment. Its maximum hydrogen price is set by the cost of making the same product, or delivering the same useful heat, another way.

In a recent development, the central 2050 scenario in my European hydrogen assessment puts on-site production at €5.70/kg. That starts with electricity at €60/MWh and 53 kWh of electricity per kilogram of hydrogen, so the electricity alone costs €3.18/kg. Electrolysers, capital recovery, maintenance, stack replacements, water and other plant costs bring the total to €5.70. Getting hydrogen to a customer can cost more.

At a factory using hydrogen for process heat, €5.70/kg is an expensive fuel. With 94% heating efficiency, delivering one MWh of useful heat requires roughly 31.9 kg of hydrogen. The fuel bill reaches €182/MWh before the burner, maintenance and other equipment costs. In the model’s central 2050 comparison, suitable direct-electric heating sets a hydrogen price ceiling of €2.07/kg. At that ceiling the same hydrogen heat costs about €66/MWh. The hydrogen production case overshoots the customer’s competitive input price by €3.63/kg.

The mismatch is not a prediction that hydrogen makers will never lower costs. It is the actual commercial test investors should apply before financing supply. Reducing the cost of production from €7 to €5 a kilogram achieves little if the relevant industrial customer can pay €2. Production-cost targets are meaningless without a corresponding market price ceiling.

The International Energy Agency’s Global Hydrogen Review 2026 has made customer cost acceptability part of its assessment. Across most sector and region comparisons, the IEA finds maximum acceptable hydrogen prices below US$2/kg without policy support. Some incumbent-steel comparisons yield negative acceptable prices. The IEA examines a 2035 horizon and a different set of competitors; the same buyer-side arithmetic exposes the problem.

It has been revealed that my TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment calculates the maximum hydrogen input price for industrial heat, ammonia and ironmaking and compares it with distinct European supply cases. It also links to the underlying European hydrogen research and interactive model.

Sources indicate that european ammonia illustrates how demand for a product differs from demand for European-made hydrogen. Ammonia remains necessary for fertilisers and industrial chemicals. The buyer’s real choice is where to produce it. In the central 2050 TFIE model, making qualifying green ammonia inside Europe can compete with imported green ammonia only when its hydrogen input costs roughly €2.62–€4.00/kg, depending on the origin and production route. The €5.70/kg onsite supply case misses those thresholds. Europe can keep consuming ammonia without building every electrolyser locally.

According to recent reports, ironmaking has a similar sourcing decision. The model’s hydrogen input-price ceiling versus qualifying imported hydrogen-reduced or hot-briquetted iron ranges from €2.28 to €4.45/kg. Against a European electrochemical iron process, the central ceiling is approximately €1.43/kg. Where enough suitable scrap can deliver the required steel grade, the hydrogen-based route can lose even at a zero price for hydrogen. Steel quality, industrial integration and the commercial maturity of electrochemical iron matter to those comparisons. They do not entitle a hydrogen supplier to ignore the alternatives.

Hydrogen used as a chemical reagent deserves a different assessment from hydrogen burned for heat. Chemical production may need the molecule. Industrial heating needs temperature, pressure, reliability and useful energy, all of which can be delivered directly from electricity for many applications. Manufacturing hydrogen from electricity and then burning it adds conversion losses and fuel-system costs before the plant receives the heat it needs.

According to recent reports, the supply cases have defined boundaries. The central onsite cost is €5.70/kg. A generic delivery allowance takes that case to €6.95/kg. The model’s separately configured hub-and-pipeline case is €5.81/kg. Those are different cost structures, not interchangeable price quotes for the same customer. Even the favourable 2050 case, at €3.46/kg with its specified delivery allowance and €28/MWh electricity, clears some industrial thresholds but still misses others.

Policy can create demand that market prices do not support. Carbon pricing, procurement mandates, subsidies and carbon contracts for difference can raise willingness or obligation to pay. That may be a deliberate industrial or climate choice, but governments should disclose the premium, who will finance it and the contract duration. Describing a regulated purchase as competitive demand hides the cost rather than eliminating it.

Industry observers note that the EU energy regulators’ market monitoring points in the same direction. ACER reported 4.2 GW of committed electrolyser capacity in November 2026, including operating plants, projects under construction and those with final investment decisions. Roughly 49% was associated with refining, where renewable-fuel mandates provide a strong demand signal. The remaining industrial sectors face a harder test when policy does not compel the same purchases.

Sources indicate that for lenders, the consequence is immediate. A proposed hydrogen plant costing €5/kg has no viable commercial case when its intended industrial buyer can afford €3/kg. A memorandum of understanding cannot close that €2/kg gap. Developers need buyers with enforceable contracts at prices that cover supply costs, lower production costs, or identified support durable enough to finance the difference.

According to recent reports, industrial and public procurement should start with the product the customer must deliver, calculate the best eligible competing route, and determine the maximum hydrogen price that route permits. Only then should investors consider electrolysers, pipelines and capacity targets. Suppliers do not set the market by drawing cheaper future cost curves. Industrial customers set the ceiling.

In a recent development, the full TFIE Briefing and open European hydrogen assessment contain the industrial route comparisons, scenario assumptions and research submitted to the European Commission. The next Briefing examines the competing routes for sourcing green ammonia and iron.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, 'Tis the season when Americans drown the last few months of hardship, like the doubled cost of car repairs and record upcoming car price highs, in gravy and egg nog and go gung-ho on buying gifts for friends and family. I tend not to partake in the yearly ritual, but if I do participate, one of my favorite gifts to give or receive is a book. Sometimes the people in your life surprise you with titles you would have never come across on your own.

The act of book-giving is actually a common practice for the Christmas Eve holiday in Iceland. "Jólabókaflóð, which translates to "Christmas Book Flood" is the practice of gifting your loved ones books on Christmas Eve. In this ever-present digital world, it's nice to be given something tangible that can be enjoyed and shared with others.

Recent findings suggest that lucky for automotive enthusiasts, there's an endless bounty of books on everything from cars to planes, to race cars and sinking ships. You name it — there's probably a book about it. So, tell us, what car-related books are you reading right now?

Thanks to my ADHD and tendency to "mood read," I have a terrible habit of starting a book, setting it down, and finishing another book instead, therefore leaving a trail of unfinished, to-be-read-later books behind. In that collection sits "Life After Cars" which I started months ago, and appear to have only finished the introduction. If you want to know more on it, Jalop Collin Woodard wrote this insightful review earlier this year. The other I truly need to finish is "Bruce McLaren, The Man and His Racing team" by Eoin S. Young. It's just shy of 200 pages of reading, so it's a light read. So far it comes off much like a parallel accompaniment to the McLaren documentary.

If I had to list the books I'm eyeing to eventually read in the near distant future, there's the coffee table book I purchased earlier this year on the Porsche 718 and 804, and also I picked up a book called "Carmageddon" which looks like it runs along similar messaging to "Life After Cars.".

Industry observers note that now, take a look at your bookshelf, end table, desk, or whatever odd place you find yourself leaving your books and tell us about the car-related books you've been reading. Our own magnificent fearless leader, Erin Marquis, is reading "Terror in the City of Champions: Murder, Baseball, and the Secret Society That Shocked Depression-Era Detroit." She says it's a gripping read about the heyday of Detroit covering sport, city, political, labor and automotive history.

If you're not reading something that hits the spot via car, racing or anything transportation-related, is there a book you've finished recently you'd like to share with your friends here? Or is there something you purchased that calls out to you every time you pass it in the room, and you can't help but go "man, I really need to read that soon?" Bring on the book recommendations!

HLTH 2026: How Whoop aims to play a bigger role in healthcare" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

LAS VEGAS—Whoop gained traction as a performance wearable used by elite athletes, professional teams and Olympians to track physiological strain and sleep.

The company has evolved into a broader clinical and digital health platform that layers medical-grade hardware, blood diagnostics, electronic health record (EHR) syncing, and physician care on top of its continuous biometric tracking. The company's FDA-cleared ECG detects signs of atrial fibrillation and allows members to share results with their healthcare provider.

It has been revealed that whoop is a screenless, wrist-worn device that measures strain, recovery and sleep 24/7, paired with Whoop Coach, an AI-powered, in-app health and fitness assistant. The manufacturer expanded its Advanced Labs testing—combining Quest blood testing, clinician reviews and AI insights—to non-members, alongside integrating Grail's multi-cancer early detection test. Whoop partners with health platform HealthEx to let consumers connect their medical records directly to the Whoop app, combining medical history with biometric data. A feature rolled out earlier this year lets Whoop members directly connect with clinicians through the app, including live, on-demand video consultations.

In a recent development, the company has raised over $900 million to date, including a $575 million series G round in March, pushing its valuation to $10 billion. Whoop told Bloomberg it looks to hire 600 people this year, a roughly 75% boost to its headcount, as it works to further integrate AI into its health and wellness monitoring tools and to expand internationally. The company is on track for an initial public offering in 18 months, executives told Bloomberg in August.

In a recent development, the company is positioning itself as a continuous health monitor that goes beyond fitness tracking. The device's 24/7 physiological data can function almost like an ongoing health check, becoming a bridge between everyday health and medical care, Will Ahmed, founder and CEO of Whoop, mentioned during an on-stage interview at HLTH on Tuesday.

Ahmed argued that the conventional annual medical physical is "frozen in time.".

According to recent reports, "The reality is wearing a continuous health monitor like Whoop that should be a 24/7 annual checkup. That's how it should function from a data standpoint," he noted during a fireside chat with Michael Phelps, U.S. former competitive swimmer, who is the most decorated Olympian in history with 23 gold medals, and also a Whoop customer since 2015.

Industry observers note that "Then there will be alerts when something is really wrong, and particularly as we combine these different data sources together, again, 24/7 physiological data, blood tests, medical records, how you're feeling and contextual cues. When we have all this information in one place, and now we've got 3.5 million members, about to be 4 million members, it's just amazing the insights that you can pull together from that. And so you can start to predict that someone may need to get a cancer screening, or may actually have a real heart problem," he said.

In a recent development, whoop can pull together biometric data, labs, medical records and information to establish a baseline for an individual, recognize meaningful changes and recommend an action. By combining continuous monitoring with information such as blood tests, the tech giant hopes to help owners piece together health signals and determine when they may need care, Ahmed remarked.

For Phelps, Whoop has shifted from being about maximizing elite athletic performance to helping him manage his health, energy and recovery around everyday life and longevity, he told the audience.

"For me, for 20-plus years, I've been trying to chase time, and now I'm just trying to be the healthiest person that I can be," Phelps remarked. "For me, the data that I get every single day, if my body isn't 100% or I'm not full go, then I take a step back and I tone down my workout. When I'm talking to my trainer, I'm taking it down a little bit, so I have enough energy and I have what I need to be a good dad, to be a good husband, to be a good worker, hard worker, whatever it is, just to be a good person.".

Whoop sees opportunities to turn deviations from an individual's baseline into actionable signals. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Phelps noted his Whoop device signaled that his temperature, respiratory rate and HRV changed, but he noted that the real benefit was that Whoop knew what normal looked like for him.

Using biometric data to recognize signals in a person's health can have broader implications, Ahmed noted, citing examples where members identified potentially serious health problems after noticing significant changes in their physiological data.

Sources indicate that "We're just starting to see all of these different maps presenting themselves, and it's very empowering. We're excited about the role that we can play with the broader health ecosystem," Ahmed remarked.

Ahmed mentioned Whoop's high user engagement and continuous monitoring can fill gaps between doctors' visits and provide clinically relevant information to care teams.

"I do believe that technology like Whoop can make the whole system much more efficient and also make a doctor's life easier if we do our jobs properly, which is again to say, how do you take all this information that's being collected about a patient or a consumer and how do you simplify it to the one, two, or three questions that a doctor might actually want to know the answer to before you show up to their office?" he stated.

Ahmed sees the AI coach evolving into a personal health companion sitting on top of a longitudinal health record.

In a recent development, "That's another area that we're really excited about, where this idea that you can have a conversation with Whoop or what feels like this entity that sits on top of your data, and all of a sudden you feel like you have a health companion, and yes, you've got 24/7 physiological data from sensors, but you can also now have your medical records. You can also now have your blood tests. There are all sorts of conversational cues. 'How are you feeling today?' 'Did you drink alcohol last night?' Were you traveling?' You put all that information together, all that data in one place, and the insights are quite profound," he remarked.

Partnerships with other digital health companies and acquisitions help Whoop broaden the platform, he noted.

"We like to think about it from the consumer's vantage point first, which is to say, if you're an individual, if you're a consumer, what is data that you want on your body or you need on your body, and that may be data that's being collected somewhere else, in which case, we feel like there could be an opportunity for a partnership," Ahmed mentioned, adding, "We're also comfortable now acquiring technology and acquiring different innovations, which has become more of a muscle that we've built over the last 12 months.".

Whoop believes its biggest strategic advantage is the consumer relationship.

Members open the app roughly eight times a day and wear the device nearly 23 hours a day.

"There are so many of us who have been in health tech where we would die for that kind of engagement, and I think that's something we're always striving for because we're an industry that was never built with the consumer in the center," noted Lynne O'Keefe, founder and manager partner of Define Ventures, who moderated the on-stage interview.

Recent findings suggest that the organization is strategically expanding into an older, more medical population. Whoop is a participant in the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services' ACCESS model. Ahmed remarked members 65 and older are actually Whoop's most highly engaged demographic, challenging the assumption that consumer health technology primarily appeals to younger people.

It has been revealed that "It's clearly a population that cares a lot about their health. They want to focus on what's going on with their blood pressure, their ECG, or whether they need to send data to their doctors," he stated.

Ahmed framed CMS' ACCESS model as a move from consumers simply paying for a wearable toward government reimbursement tied to measurable health outcomes, such as improvements in blood pressure or weight.

Industry observers note that "I think as a model of innovation for a government and its citizens, it's pretty interesting because it incentivizes companies to actually create technology or programs that are making people healthier. It should change the cost curve because you're paying if that outcome is delivered, and then to the consumer, you're both hopefully being healthier and not paying for a product that otherwise would have had to," he said.

In a recent development, whoop also positions itself as a platform that can wrap around drugs and other healthcare interventions. The company announced this week a partnership with Novo Nordisk as part of the pharma company's redesign of its direct-to-consumer NovoCare program. Novo Nordisk relaunched its NovoCare direct-to-consumer program. Patients taking a GLP-1 can integrate wearable data from Whoop as part of their program.

Whoop can function as a potential companion for GLP-1 people, monitoring exercise, sleep, resting heart rate, HRV and other signals while helping users preserve health and fitness during treatment, Ahmed said.

When asked about the future vision for Whoop, he mentioned, "I think in simple terms, it's our responsibility to build technology that either makes you healthier or one day saves your life. You're going to have all of this health data on your body. I think organizing that information in one place, alongside 24/7 wearable data, and alongside a powerful AI that can sit on top of that data and go off on your behalf and take actions and schedule appointments with the doctor, or go speak to your doctor on your behalf, or alert you when something's wrong," he said.

He added, "God forbid this day comes, but you should wake up and be told from Whoop you need to go to the doctor in the next 30 minutes, and it's been scheduled, and you show up, and all of a sudden you find out that you're having a heart attack, or you're having some serious life event. To me, that feels like an inevitable future, and I do predict that a large percentage of humanity in the future will be wearing a continuous health monitor.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heather Rae El Moussa and Christine Quinn are set to make their highly anticipated return to “Selling Sunset,” and while both women say the time since they’ve last been on the show has been transformative, it appears they still have unresolved issues to iron out.

Netflix dropped the Season 10 trailer on Nov. 18, and in one heated exchange, Christine and Heather’s conflict comes to a head.

Sources indicate that the pair have been at odds for quite some time, facing multiple tense on-screen moments. In a 2023 E! News interview, Christine branded Heather “a snooze fest,” claiming she’s not interesting enough for TV.

Then, in a July 2026 clip from E!, Heather revealed that prior to filming Season 10, she had not seen or spoken to Christine in four years.

“You literally said you hated me,” Christine pressed in the trailer.

Instead of shying away from the confrontation, Heather fessed up.

“At that point, Christine, I did,” she admitted.

In another scene, Heather opens up to her husband, Tarek El Moussa, sharing insight on the challenging dynamic between the women.

“It was a big decision for me to even start working in the office again,” said Heather, noting that “obviously,” she has her “guard up” with Christine and still feels she can’t “trust her.”.

Sources indicate that “She’s gone through some sh-t,” Tarek responded. “That previous Christine is still this newly introduced Christine.”.

Despite the tension, both women seem to be excited for the upcoming season, which premieres on Dec. 4.

In a since-expired Instagram Story, Heather noted, “The trailer is so good. I watched it like 10 times.”.

Christine meanwhile wrote “We’re SOOO back!” in a comment on a Netflix post sharing a condensed-version of the trailer.

Both women opened up to Netflix’s publication, Tudum, ahead of the latest season.

“I finally feel secure enough in who I am to walk back into that world and not lose myself in it,” Heather said.

In a recent development, the proud mom left The Oppenheim Group after Season 7 to focus on family after welcoming her first child with Tarek—a son named Tristan Jay, now 3. Heather is also a co-parent to her husband’s two older children, Taylor Reese, 16, and Brayden James, 11, whom he shares with his ex-wife, Christina Haack.

“I want people to see the full picture of who I am now,” she continued. “Not just the dramatic moments. The version of me returning is very different from the one who left.”.

In the interview, Heather teased, “there are conversations that got cut short,” that there are some things she’s “not going to pretend” haven’t happened.

Meanwhile, Christine parted ways with the brokerage at the end of Season 5, after welcoming her son, Christian Georges Dumontet, whom she shares with her estranged husband, Christian Dumontet.

“Motherhood has a way of sharpening your priorities and changing how you move through the world,” she told Tudum. “I’ve become more intentional and much more protective of my peace.”.

With that mentioned, Christine doesn’t plan to steer clear of all conflict.

“I’m still ambitious and direct, but I think people will see a version of me that’s more centered and even more sure of herself,” she explained. “I’m hoping this chapter feels fresh and honest.”.

It has been revealed that season 10 will also see the return of agents Bre Tiesi and Amanza Smith. Four latest professionals will join the group, too: Jordyn Taylor, Sasha Lance, Sonni Pacheco, and Tara Burns.

According to recent reports, jason Oppenheim, head of the brokerage, said, “The newly introduced agents have already shaken up the office, but in a good way. I absolutely love the new ladies, and they make me excited about the future here at the brokerage and on the show.”.

#64997. EV Share Jumps to 68%(!) and Small BEVs Rise to Power — China EV Sales Report for October

EV Share Jumps to 68%(!) and Small BEVs Rise to Power — China EV Sales Report for October

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • High gas prices and a never-ending wave of upcoming BEVs have allowed October to reach 68% EV market share, a new record!
  • Sources indicate that this record achievement is thanks to a significant ICE (internal combustion engine) crash.
  • In a recent development, adding 45% BEV share to PHEVs (23% share) meant that in October a record 68% of all cars sold in China had a plug!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

High gas prices and a never-ending wave of upcoming BEVs have allowed October to reach 68% EV market share, a new record!

Sources indicate that this record achievement is thanks to a significant ICE (internal combustion engine) crash. The overall market dropped 27% year over year (YoY), to around 1.6 million sales. Plugins were down 14% YoY, but pure ICE sales were much worse off, crashing 44% YoY!

In a recent development, adding 45% BEV share to PHEVs (23% share) meant that in October a record 68% of all cars sold in China had a plug! If this trend continues in the future, the Chinese market will be fully electrified by 2030, and will be 100% BEV before 2035!

Recent findings suggest that this great result pulled the 2026 share up, to 59%, already 5% above the full year result of 2025. BEVs on their own were up to 40% (versus 33% in 2025).

It has been revealed that at this pace, I expect the final number for 2026 EV share in China to be above 60%, with BEVs alone north of the 40% mark. And when the largest global automotive market gets this electrified … then the ICE industry is in serious trouble.

Industry observers note that the ICE extinction is also visible in the overall ranking. The overall top 10 was fully made by EVs. Again.

It has been revealed that looking at the best sellers in several size categories, the ICE extinction is also quite visible. Although, once again, the C-segment/compact category is the exception, with the only ICE representative showing up there — the Toyota RAV4, in 2nd, behind the leader Nevo Q05 and just ahead of the BYD Dolphin.

Having a quick look at the five size categories, the highlight is the B-segment/subcompact category, which is the hottest segment right now, with three of the top four top sellers in October belonging to this category.

Considering that 56% of the new SUVs launched this year were bigger than 5 meters/197 inches, there is a clear disconnect between what people want (small hatchbacks/crossovers) and what OEMs offer (large SUVs).

Another highlight is the fact that Xiaomi had a gold plus silver win in the full size category, with the BYD Great Tang closing out the podium while the midsize category podium was 100% BYD Group.

Here’s more info and commentary on October’s top selling electric models:.

According to recent reports, A BYD Dolphin for BYD Seagull money ($10,000). This was Geely’s internal memo to describe the formula for the Geely Xingyuan when developing its star model. With an interesting name — Xingyuan translates as “wishing upon a star” — it seems that Geely had its wish granted. However, the Geely model will have a tough adversary soon, as the new generation Seagull will land with only one goal — to steal the Xingyuan’s best seller status. But while the new Seagull didn’t land, the small Geely scored a record performance in October, with its 50,190 registrations representing a 14% increase YoY. Besides the new BYD Seagull, Geely’s hatchback now has to deal with Leapmotor’s B-segment contenders, the A10 and A05; the new-generation Wuling Bingo; Chery’s new QQ3; and let’s not forget about BYD’s Yuan Up, too.

According to recent reports, BYD’s midsize SUV continues to transition into the latest generation. Thanks to the ramp-up of the new Ultra body, BYD’s star player was 2nd, scoring 30,772 registrations. Sales were up by 6% compared to the same month last year. The new Ultra generation features lidar and 1,500 kW DC charging, and these two features aren’t even the most impressive aspects of the model! That would be the price. It starts at 152,000 yuan (or $22,000) with the 76 kWh battery, and it goes up to 180,000 yuan (or $26,000) with the 83 kWh battery. For comparison, the Tesla Model Y starts in China at 259,000 yuan ($38,250)…. Expect the Song to experience a second youth from here onwards, and while it is impossible to displace the Tesla Model Y from the runner-up spot, the last place on the podium is doable this year. And maybe higher up in 2027?

According to recent reports, BYD’s small crossover continues to surprise, thanks to recently improved specs. BYD’s team player rose to 3rd in October, scoring 28,514 registrations, which was a 44% increase YoY and a latest record score. Despite not being the most exciting vehicle to look at, or drive, the truth is that it is surfing the wave of small, affordable EVs better than most, scoring high in value for money with prices starting at $11,000 and higher end versions having BYD’s driver-assistance system. With small vehicles presently having a moment in China, expect the small crossover to show up in the top 5 more regularly.

Sources indicate that things continue to go well for the startup brand, with its fresh baby A10 now established as the star player in an already strong lineup. Thanks to 27,247 registrations, the small crossover managed another top 5 presence. The model has the usual value-for-money focus of the brand, and a low, low price of 66,000 yuan ($10,000). On top of that, however, the A10 offers something close to a distinct personality, as the design eschews the white product standard design of Leapmotor for something more personal, mostly thanks to the front and back lights and a floating roof effect. With B-segment BEVs now being the hottest category in China, Leapmotor is well prepared to benefit from the subcompact rising tide, thanks to the recent arrival of the A10 small crossover and its sibling, the A05 small hatchback. Talk about perfect timing….

After the SU7 and YU7, Xiaomi has another success on its hands. This significant fat SUV — or shall I say SUVs, as the lineup is broken down between the 7-seat N90 and the 5-seat N70 — scored 27,132 registrations in only its second month on the market, pulling it immediately into the overall top 5. Even with the number of competitors growing every passing day, Xiaomi’s latest land yachts have been selling like hot cakes, while drying up sales of the competition. Proof of that, is the fact that there were only two full size models in October’s top 20, with the other being … the Xiaomi SU7.

Sources indicate that looking at the rest of the best seller table, there were a number of models hitting record scores, starting with the #8 Nevo Q05 (20,022 units) continuing its success story. The #10 Bestune Xiaoma (17,887 units) benefitted from a recent refresh to score a surprise record score. Could this mean that small city EVs are (finally) seeing the light at the end of the tunnel?

According to recent reports, as for the second half of the table, the highlight is the ramp-up of the Xpeng L03, with the attractive looking crossover, which kind of reminds of a mini-Lotus or small Polestar, reaching 13th thanks to 15,653 sales. This EV looks to be the startup’s star model thanks to a competitive price (124,000 RMB) that is half the price of the Tesla Model Y!

Other models with record performances were the #14 MG 4 (15,503 units), with the newly introduced generation proving to be much more popular and adaptable to local tastes than the previous one, and the #17 Chery QQ3 EV, which continued its slow climb in the ranking thanks to 14,041 sales, which made it the 5th B-segment model in the top 20.

Industry observers note that still in the top 20, we should also highlight the best selling foreign model, the Tesla Model Y VW ID.Aura T6, the newly introduced China-made (and China-developed) German crossover that has allowed Volkswagen to beat the Texans for the first time in years (the Tesla Model Y was down 60% YoY, to 7,807 units, while the Model 3 was down 85%, to 1,010 units). The Aura T6, VW’s take on the Model Y formula, rose to the 20th position in its first full month on the market!

A promising sign, or just hype? Only time will tell, but at least for now, VW seems to be getting some traction on the EV side of the Chinese market, a point also highlighted by the fact that it wasn’t just the Aura T6 getting decent sales. The also new VW ID.Era 5S (think Chinese VW Jetta) got 7,100 registrations in October. Is there hope after all?

Outside the top 20, the main event was the ramp-up of Nevo’s latest baby, the Q06, which is looking to replicate the Q05’s success in the category above. With some 10,000 registrations in only its second month, it looks like it could join the top 20 soon. The same can be noted about the Geely Galaxy TT, the make’s answer to the Xiaomi SU7, which had around 10,500 deliveries in October. Then there’s also the BYD Yuan Plus, which, after a long cross through the desert, seems to be picking up steam again. It scored 11,658 registrations last month, a new year best.

It has been revealed that looking at the 2026 ranking, the podium remained the same, and unless something unexpected happens, it should stay as it is until the end of the year, with the small Geely repeating its 2025 win. That also means the Tesla Model Y will return to silver after getting bronze in 2025, and the BYD Song will get back onto the podium after a one-year absence.

Recent findings suggest that below the podium positions, though, there was some news. The BYD Yuan Up and Leapmotor A10 are surfing the B-segment wave and both climbed a position, to 5th and 6th, respectively.

If the BYD Yuan Up continues on its current record streak, then the small crossover could even aim to surpass the #4 FCB Ti7 before the year ends.

Still, with three subcompacts presently in the top 6 (Geely Xingyuan, BYD Yuan Up, and Leapmotor A10), small is hot right now, in China.

Elsewhere, the BYD Sealion 05 was up two positions, to 16th, while the Wuling Mini EV is hoping to bring tiny city cars back into the spotlight, and in October, it jumped two positions, ending the month in 13th….

Looking at the overall manufacturer ranking, it is a sea of red. Everyone is losing sales — big time. The exception is #5 Leapmotor (+31% YoY), while #8 Xiaomi (+3% YoY) and #10 Xpeng (+0%) are just hanging on.

So, now, not only are foreign OEMs suffering (Nissan was down 70% in October, Honda was down 51%), but even domestic ones are being affected by the EV shift.

Some may be asking, “But what about #9 Nevo and its 125% growth rate?” Well, it isn’t so much that they are winning sales, but they are effectively replacing the sales of their mother brand, Changan, which in October was only 19th after a 60% drop in sales YoY.

Looking at the auto brand ranking, BYD is firmly in the leadership position (17.2%), while runner-up Geely held to its 7.1% market share.

Rising 3rd placed Leapmotor (6.7%, up 0.2%) is fast approaching Geely. It wouldn’t be surprising if the startup brand became the newly introduced silver medalist in the final days of the year.

Sources indicate that one thing is for certain though — Leapmotor will win its first medal this year. The only question is the material that it will be made of….

Sources indicate that speaking of position changes, Tesla had a horrible month (4.4%, down from 4.9% in September), which allowed Wuling (4.6%) to climb one position in October, into 4th. At the end of the year, expect Tesla to keep the #4 position, as its December peak should help it surpass Wuling.

Looking at OEMs/automotive groups/alliances, BYD is leading with 21.9% share of the market, up 0.1% in October.

Meanwhile, Geely remained in second with 11.8% share. The multinational conglomerate has the runner-up spot secured.

Sources indicate that #3 SAIC was stable (8%) and remained firm in the last place on the podium, while #4 Leapmotor (6.7%, up 0.2%) remained on the rise. Will we see the startup challenge SAIC in 2027 for the 3rd spot?

Latest Update: Every Car Brand Has To Install Seat Belts, But Wearing Them Still Isn't Universally Mandated

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (839 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Buckling a seat belt is second nature, or it should be.
  • Recent findings suggest that early iterations of the seat belt were developed in the 19th century and intended for aircraft.
  • According to recent reports, in 1984, Newly introduced York became the first state to make seat belt use mandatory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Buckling a seat belt is second nature, or it should be. Once the car door is closed, next comes that click of confirmation. But safety belts were introduced long, long, long after 1769, when the first car ever made came into existence. Not that seat belts were an afterthought; they simply weren't thought of at all. Not for cars, anyway.

Recent findings suggest that early iterations of the seat belt were developed in the 19th century and intended for aircraft. Seat belts weren't added to consumer cars until 1949, when Wisconsin-based Nash Motors Manufacturer introduced them. Still, not until 1968 were seat belts federally mandated for every seating position in passenger cars. This standard was later amended to include buses and trucks; however, this was merely a manufacturing requirement. Actual seat belt usage and enforcement were left to the states. Because of this, there remains one state that doesn't require adults to wear a seat belt: New Hampshire.

According to recent reports, in 1984, Newly introduced York became the first state to make seat belt use mandatory. The exceptions were children who, depending on age and weight, are to be secured either in a child safety seat or booster. Keep in mind that Volvo, the maven of automotive safety, introduced the three-point seat belt in 1959. Despite evidence showing seat belts not only minimize injuries but also save lives, automotive safety systems receive plenty of pushback, at least initially.

Sources indicate that following New York's lead, other states enacted seat belt laws throughout the '80s and '90s. Maine was the last state to make seat belt use required, putting its law into effect in late 1995. In the decades since, New Hampshire has remained a holdout, though its nonchalance toward seat belts is strictly an adult matter, to be fair.

According to recent reports, all other states and the District of Columbia require front-seat occupants to buckle up. For backseat passengers, only 34 states and D.C. say it's a must. And kids being kids have different rules entirely. Some states necessitate seat belt use for front occupants only. Others require that each person be clicked in, regardless of seat location. For children, because standard seat belts cannot properly restrain them during a crash, we've got car seats, booster seats, and other safety equipment to consider.

The rules in New Hampshire do account for minors, requiring occupants younger than 18, including teen drivers, to be properly fastened. There are exceptions, though. Children don't need to be buckled if they're riding in a vehicle built before 1968 (or in a bus or taxi), have a physical condition that prevents seat belt use, or fall under certain special-education conditions. Everyone else? They take the state's motto of "Live Free or Die" to heart.

Industry observers note that according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, seat belts reduce serious injuries and deaths by about 50%, and saved nearly 15,000 lives in 2017. Before seat belt use became law, only 14% of people wore them. Usage increased to 59% within a decade. In 2025, 92% of drivers and 90% of front-seat passengers buckled up, according to the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety. But in New Hampshire, less than 80% of travelers bother to buckle.

According to recent reports, fresh Hampshire authorities are aware of this less-than-stellar safety record. The New Hampshire Office of Highway Safety (NHOHS) promotes "Join the NH Clique," which coincides with NHTSA's nationwide Click It or Ticket seat belt enforcement campaign. Law enforcement takes a no-excuses approach during the program, but they might as well be yelling at clouds from their front porch because it achieves the same effect. After all, police can't write tickets when a law hasn't been broken.

The state legislature has tried multiple times to introduce bills requiring seat belts for all, but every effort failed. A 2023 attempt was even soft-pitched as a secondary offense. Had the bill passed, actual usage would have depended on whether seat belt violations were treated as primary or secondary offenses. As of November 2026, just 35 states and D.C. have primary enforcement laws, and numbers support that reasoning. Nevertheless, whether old-timey lap belts or innovative multi-adaptive safety belts (another Volvo invention), no amount of safety tech matters unless people are compelled to wear them.

The National Safety Council (NSC) compiled NHTSA data from 2024 that indicated seat belt usage at 91.2%, yet unbuckled occupants accounted for 48.4% of passenger vehicle deaths. Among 21- to 34-year-olds, about 60% of occupants killed weren't buckled. The NSC notes that in California — where seat belt use is a primary-enforced law for everyone aged 16 and up – observed usage in the front seats was 97.5% and unrestrained occupants accounted for 43% of occupant deaths. North Dakota, which only switched to primary enforcement in 2023, saw 79.8% usage while unbelted occupants accounted for 53% of deaths. The statistics from Latest Hampshire are more somber, showing only 78.2% wear their belts, while unbelted occupants accounted for 59% of deaths.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Longevity platform Hone Health nabs $228M to build out offerings" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Hone Health, a physician-led virtual longevity care platform, has raised $228 million.

In a recent development, the investment is structured as a combination of equity and growth financing. The $28 million series A extension was led by MarcyPen Capital Partners, with participation from Pentland Ventures, Kinship Ventures, Hanwha, Gannet Capital, humbition and Comma Capital. Other angel investors also participated, including the Jonas brothers. The $200 million in growth financing came from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

According to recent reports, hone will use the investment to support a number of expansions. It intends to launch more programming for metabolic health, PMOS, inflammation and immunity, and to launch a physician-supervised peptide program. It will add more diagnostics, including coronary CT angiography and gut microbiome analysis.

Recent findings suggest that hone also plans to continue building out its AI operating system that brings data together to help personalize care. And it plans to build out clinical trial infrastructure to support pharma partners.

“Longevity is thought of as this super exotic thing. […] I actually think longevity is now becoming primary care,” Saad Alam, co-founder and CEO of Hone, told Fierce Healthcare.

It costs $65 to test for 70 biomarkers with Hone, followed by a clinician consult with the option to add more diagnostics. Labs, health history, symptoms and medications are run through its AI, which then gives providers treatment recommendations. Hone can keep adding additional diagnostics and medications, per Alam, “and the AI gets smarter as we get more patients into that system.”.

Industry observers note that additionally, Hone is publicly announcing Hone Black, a fresh concierge longevity membership that has operated in stealth for a select group of patients for the past year. It combines diagnostics on over 1,600 health markers with ongoing medical care from physicians. Offerings include prescriptions, supplements, peptides and lifestyle guidance, plus exosome and stem cell therapies.

It has been revealed that alam founded the firm after experiencing a shift in his health at 35 years old, including mental health complications, depression and weight gain. His doctor was initially of little help. It took Alam a year to find out he had low testosterone, and after treatment, he finally felt back on track. That experience, along with his father dying from kidney disease and his mother going through early menopause, opened his eyes to the longevity space.

It has been revealed that “This whole concept of longevity is going to be one of the single greatest problems I can dedicate my life to solving,” Alam realized at the time. He experimented with everything, from peptides to cold plunges to meditation.

It has been revealed that hone is a subsidiary of Time Therapeutics, which aims to support production of drugs that help people live longer. Alam, who started his career doing market research at Eli Lilly, knew clinical trials are expensive and inaccessible. He wanted to create a firm that could help commercialize drugs. The first step to that is Hone, or a DTC virtual care company that can capture longitudinal data on patients. The next phase will be publishing research. Finally, Hone will look to partner with pharma to get drugs to market faster.

The manufacturer has been providing care for five years, treating about 200,000 patients to date. It requires patients to have a physician and get bloodwork every 90 days in order to get medication refills. Members can contact their clinician between sessions as needed.

“We make sure, for the most part, that you are doing bloodwork and talking to a physician, a real conversation with a physician, in order to get prescribed medication,” Alam said.

Recent findings suggest that it isn’t about overprescribing medications. It’s about finding the most personalized protocol for each patient. “The companies that have—no pun intended—longevity are the ones that are going to figure out how to reduce the number of medications somebody might need,” Alam remarked.

Sources indicate that hone began with hormone therapy, then moved into longevity care with biomarker analysis and women’s health. Two months ago, Hone’s offerings for women surpassed offerings for men in terms of net new members. It soon plans to run clinical trials on poly-chronic patients as well to help determine the right drug at the right time. Hone crossed $100 million in revenue in 2025, per Alam, and is on track to double this year.

“When I started goop, wellness was a niche conversation,” Gwyneth Paltrow, founder and CEO of goop and co-founder of Kinship Ventures, said in a press release. “Today, it’s one of the biggest categories in the world, and the next step is bringing real health and wellness to the masses, not just the few. Saad has built Hone to do exactly that, with serious science and at real scale. That’s why Kinship invested, and we could not be more excited about what’s ahead.”.

Hone will soon offer 14 longevity care categories, which Alam argues is akin to primary care. He estimates that Hone only refers to in-person care about 10% of the time, usually for higher-acuity conditions. Some Hone patients are already healthy; most are sick and willing to pay out of pocket because the current system has been inadequate in solving their health needs, per Alam.

Sources indicate that “This is just the beginning of not only a way but a complete change in the way that medicine is practiced,” Alam said. “A lot of other companies are what I’ll call pill mills, and where we’ve really focused—our energy is making sure that we go through the more difficult work of managing the long-term health of our patients.”.

Industry News: The Legendary 1987 RUF CTR 'Yellowbird' Looks Like A Porsche, But It Isn't

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Take a quick look at that yellow beast in our top photo, with its bulging muscular fenders, curved profile, and massive whale tail spoiler.
  • According to recent reports, there are a couple of dead giveaways, too, including the fact that the Yellowbird could outrun any real production Porsches of the time.
  • Sources indicate that of course, peeking under the skin of the Yellowbird tells the tale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Take a quick look at that yellow beast in our top photo, with its bulging muscular fenders, curved profile, and massive whale tail spoiler. Now, you could easily be forgiven for thinking it was a Porsche — perhaps a late-1980s 911 Carrera 3.2. You'd be wrong, however. That machine is actually a Ruf CTR, which was nicknamed the Yellowbird for its striking exterior finish.

According to recent reports, there are a couple of dead giveaways, too, including the fact that the Yellowbird could outrun any real production Porsches of the time. In fact, a Ruf CTR beat all challengers at a famed 1987 Road & Track comparison of the fastest cars in the world: Its 211-mph top speed was 10 mph faster than the second-place car, which was a modified Porsche, while entries like the AMG Hammer, Ferrari Testarossa, Lamborghini Countach, and Porsche 959 all failed to reach 200 mph. Unsurprisingly, the CTR was also named one of our readers' favorite yellow cars of all time.

Sources indicate that of course, peeking under the skin of the Yellowbird tells the tale. Keep in mind that Ruf is much more than just a tuning shop or an in-house performance brand, like Mercedes' AMG was and now is. Ruf uses so many proprietary components — and so few from production Porsche models — that it was certified as a full-on automaker back in 1981. Ruf cars even have different W09 VINs from Porsche's WP0 vehicle identification numbers. The genesis, though, actually does start with a Mercedes-Benz — well, that and a Porsche 356.

It has been revealed that the tech giant now known as Ruf — pronounced roof – began when Alois Ruf Sr. opened his first repair shop in Pfaffenhausen, Germany, in 1939. Ruf and the shop would both survive World War II, and in the 1950s, he expanded into building his own tour bus — on a chassis originally sourced from Mercedes-Benz.

According to recent reports, it was in 1963, when Ruf was at the wheel of his bus, that he happened to see a driver lose control of his Porsche 356 and run off the road. Ruf then played a key role in bringing both back to health: He drove the Porsche's owner to the hospital and — after buying it off of the insurer — took the car itself back to his shop to fix. That began a lifelong romance between the Rufs and rear-engined Porsches, and one that carried over to the launch of the 911. Today, 911s like the Carrera GTS T-Hybrid are still out there making the haters look real dumb.

We're going to skip a lot of steps in a pretty fascinating story, but Alois Jr. took over for his father in 1974 after the latter died. Under Alois Jr.'s direction, and in response to rumors Porsche would kill off the 911 after introducing the front-engine 928, the tech giant committed itself to supporting the 911 even if Porsche didn't. The first Ruf-tuned 911, the Turbo 3.3, premiered in 1977 with a Ruf-built 5-speed manual transmission. However, legal worries soon reared their ugly heads. Porsche, naturally, wasn't too keen on being liable for what Ruf did to its cars, so Ruf would go on to officially become an independent automaker in 1981.

Yet, the car that really put Ruf on the map was the 1987 CTR, with a name derived from "Group C Turbo Ruf." The car started life as a 930-series 911 Carrera with a 3.2-liter flat-six engine, which was already one of the lightest models on the Porsche roster — it just wasn't light enough for Ruf. The organization swapped out the production doors, engine cover, and bumpers to save more poundage. The car even has just one sideview mirror. The rear fenders also were reworked, with flares to handle its upsized tire/wheel package and NACA ducts for engine cooling.

Sources indicate that ruf increased the bore of the Carrera's donor engine as well, boosting displacement to 3.4 liters. Remember, bore and stroke are the two specs that decide an engine's power. Next up were twin-turbochargers custom made for the Yellowbird and Bosch fuel injectors to slake the motor's thirst. The result was 469 horsepower and 408 pound-feet of torque. The 1987 Porsche 959, for some perspective, came out with a twin-turbo 2.8-liter flat-six factory rated for 444 horsepower and 369 pound-feet of torque.

The differences were even more noticeable on the track, as mentioned above. We'll also add that while the 959 was a tenth quicker to 60, at 3.6 seconds, the CTR could keep on going to reach 100 mph in 7.3 seconds. That's 1.5 seconds quicker than the 959. But if you really want to get a feel for what the Yellowbird was all about, be sure to check out Weissach Group's video of Ruf driver Stefan Roser running one at Nürburgring in 1989. It's downright fascinating.

Is There Any Point In Upgrading Exhaust Tips Beyond Appearance?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Exhaust tips are the most visible parts of a car's exhaust system, making them a worthwhile option if you want to personalize your ride without spending a substantial chunk of cash on a complete aftermarket exhaust setup — especially if you don't want to risk voiding your warranty and ruining the mental peace of your neighbors. Available in different shapes, sizes, materials, and finishes, aftermarket exhaust tips can lend a sportier or more premium appearance to the car they're fitted to.

Recent findings suggest that that stated, some believe that in addition to the aesthetic uplift, aftermarket tips can produce a deeper or louder exhaust note, help direct hot exhaust gases away from the rear bumper, and even improve your car's performance by reducing backpressure. What's fact, what's fiction, and do these benefits justify upgrading your car's factory exhaust tips?

The short answer is that aftermarket exhaust tips can offer some practical advantages, but they have next to no impact on performance and only a subtle effect on sound, at best. To understand what you gain from replacing them, it is notable to distinguish between the exhaust tip and the components that actually determine how an exhaust system works.

In a recent development, unlike the muffler, resonator, or catalytic converter, the exhaust tip doesn't really play a big role in controlling exhaust noise, emissions, or gas flow through your car's exhaust system. Its primary purpose is to finish the exhaust outlet, which is why aftermarket tips are available in several designs. These include straight-cut, angle-cut, rolled-edge, dual-exit, turndown, resonated, and dual-wall tips. Owners can also choose between finishes like polished stainless steel, chrome, matte black, and carbonfiber-like materials. Most aftermarket exhaust tips are pretty straightforward to install, with clamp-on and slip-on designs that directly attach to the existing tailpipe.

Industry observers note that there can be a minor change in exhaust sound, depending on the tip's diameter, length, shape, and the material used. A larger outlet may produce a somewhat deeper tone, while a longer tip can make your exhaust sound a little bit softer. A turndown tip directs exhaust gases and sound toward the ground, whereas a resonated tip can help reduce raspiness. To sum up, don't expect an aftermarket exhaust tip to make your daily-driver Toyota Camry sound like a V8-powered Lexus RC F.

Sources indicate that one possible practical upside to an aftermarket exhaust tip is that it can help direct hot exhaust gases away from the bumper and surrounding body panels, and reduce soot accumulation around the outlet (particularly if you drive a diesel car), provided it is correctly sized and positioned. Stainless steel tips can additionally offer better rust resistance than some factory exhaust tips.

Sources indicate that despite what the marketing for some aftermarket exhaust tips may suggest, using them does not deliver a noticeable increase in power, torque, or overall performance. A common misconception is that a larger-diameter tip reduces exhaust backpressure, reducing the strain on the engine and thereby producing more power. However, since the tip is only the final outlet of the exhaust system, it has no effect on the system's overall flow characteristics. The diameter, length, and layout of the exhaust pipes, along with the design of the catalytic converter, muffler, and resonator, have a much greater impact.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for more noticeable changes in sound or performance, your best bet is to upgrade other components of the exhaust system. A performance muffler can deliver a more aggressive exhaust note and reduce backpressure, while an aftermarket resonator can give you finer control over sound. A cat-back exhaust system replaces the components from the catalytic converter to the tailpipe and can also offer a substantial change in sound and performance by dialing up the exhaust flow. Upgraded headers and high-flow catalytic converters are a couple more viable options to get a more aggressive exhaust note and boost performance.

That said, these modifications are considerably more expensive than an aftermarket exhaust tip, and may affect emissions compliance and noise levels, possibly even put you in trouble with the law. On the other hand, an exhaust tip is relatively cheap (prices start at around $20) and easy to install, and worth the effort if you want a better-looking rear end, a more durable exhaust outlet, or a minor change in sound. Just don't expect it to deliver the performance and aural benefits of a proper aftermarket exhaust system.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tesla CEO Elon Musk made headlines yet again last week, when he publicly denied any affiliation with US President Donald Trump’s “MAGA” movement. If Musk intends to stage a sort of political recovery, he still has a long way to go. Denial is just a precursor to recovery, which begins in earnest when you stop denying the reality of your situation and start admitting you need help from a higher power or some such. And in fact, a higher power is coming for Musk —  if not in spiritual form, then in the form of Congress, where the incoming Democratic majority plans to exercise its authority, and call Musk to account for manipulating SpaceX satellite services in Ukraine.

During an interview for the New York Times DealBook Summit last week, Elon Musk claimed that he was not affiliated with MAGA, though he did not apologize for supporting MAGA candidates this year, or for supporting Donald Trump in 2024. Musk simply mentioned he “felt foolish” for wasting his money on losers.

Industry observers note that in the same interview, Musk insisted — falsely — that Russia was the aggrieved party when Russian President Vladimir Putin invaded the Donbas region of Ukraine back in 2014. Justin sayin’….

For those of you wondering why Elon Musk’s politics should be a matter of concern to CleanTechnica, that’s a good question, and here’s the answer: Elon Musk sailed into clean tech history on the coattails of the EV startup Tesla Motors (soon to become simply Tesla) in the early 2000’s, only to emerge in more recent years as a champion of the far right alongside President Donald Trump’s notoriously racist, fossil fuel-supporting “Make America Great Again” movement, thereby setting back the US decarbonization movement by years if not decades.

Musk has also made his own contribution to the resurgence of fossil fuels in the US. His fresh xAI data centers are well known for deploying loosely regulated (or illegal) on-site gas generators, and his SpaceX venture has been gobbling up natural gas for rocket fuel while laying plans for future expansion.

So much for Elon Musk’s footprint on the US energy profile. Let’s move over to Ukraine, where rich fossil energy and mineral resources in the nation’s Donbas region prompted Russian President Putin to send unmarked soldiers — aka the “little green men” — to annex that portion of Ukraine in 2014. A ceasefire temporarily calmed the situation until February of 2022, when Putin sent a fully equipped convoy to the Ukrainian capital city Kyiv, aiming to take over the entire seat of government in one fell swoop — literally, in one day.

Recent findings suggest that the effort failed, both militarily and in terms of Putin’s energy goals. Ukraine promptly cut Russia off from its electricity grid and hooked up with the European grid, a complex effort assisted by the Biden administration. Ukraine also set the wheels in motion to join the European Union as a significant source of clean energy, including green hydrogen gas alongside its copious potential for clean power including biomass, wind, and solar power.

To put that into perspective, consider that Ukraine is almost 90% as large as Texas, which has staked out a leadership position in wind and solar power among the 50 US states.

With Ukraine as a leading renewable energy supplier, the EU would have a fresh opportunity to meets its decarbonization goals on schedule while also reducing imports of fossil energy from Russia… And… Well… That’s where Elon Musk enters the picture.

Musk first emerged as a full blown MAGA supporter in 2020, when he helped Trump stir up conspiracy theories and confusion over the federal response to the COVID-19 crisis, in a failed effort to support the President’s bid for re-election that year. Had Trump won, he would have continued to implement a key part of his foreign policy agenda, namely, withdrawing the US from NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Alliance. NATO formed in 1949 as an effort to curb Russian expansion in Europe, an effort Trump has upended on account of his longstanding friendship with Putin.

Industry observers note that the election of Joe Biden in 2020 did not prevent Musk from providing additional aid and comfort to Trump. Musk used his media-grabbing public profile to undercut the authority of President Biden at every opportunity, including on the world stage as well as here at home. The stream of insults extended into January of 2022, even as the reality of a fresh round of Russian expansion into Europe began to materialize.

Musk had an additional opportunity to challenge Biden’s authority in January of 2022, when the so-called “Freedom Convoy” of truckers barricaded government offices in Canada, ostensibly in protest of a vaccine mandate. Musk gleefully cheered the effort, which disrupted transportation systems and distracted public attention in two key NATO allies — Canada and the US — even as Russia began ratcheting up its aims to take over Kyiv.

In a recent development, however, once it became clear that Putin’s one-day takeover of Ukraine was a failure, Musk about-faced. He took credit for providing “free” communications aid to Ukraine in the form of satellite services through the Starlink branch of SpaceX.

In a recent development, JK! A later assessment revealed that other sources shouldered about 85% of the cost of Starlink terminals initially supplied to Ukraine, including USAID here in the US (not a typo — that’s the US Administration for International Development, the same agency that Musk later destroyed in 2025).

Industry observers note that poland and other groups also contributed initial assistance to purchase  the terminals alongside an estimated 30% of connectivity costs. In addition, by September of 2022 Musk was making the case for US taxpayers to foot the bill.

It has been revealed that don’t just take my word for it. In 2023, the Belfer Center for International Affairs at Harvard recapped SpaceX’s negotiations over payment for its services to Ukraine during the previous year, concluding that “we can assume the U.S. government agreed to pay some, if not all, of the costs for continued operation of the technology.”.

“SpaceX, and particularly Musk, was able to play the role of wartime hero, showcasing the power and value of the technology products the manufacturer developed, while simultaneously avoiding sustained and hefty bills,” Belfer Center observed.

US Department of Defense contract or not, by 2023 SpaceX was already making unilateral decisions that restricted Ukraine’s ability to deploy the technology, with SpaceX CEO Gwynne Shotwell publicly insisting that the company never intended for Ukraine to use it “for offensive purposes.”.

In a recent development, of course, “offensive” is in the eye of the beholder. Since Ukraine is the invaded party seeking to assert its rights over internationally recognized borders against Russia, one could argue that every action Ukraine takes is a defensive one until Putin agrees to concede defeat and cede back his illegal claims over Ukrainian lands.

Industry observers note that of course, that’s not how Musk portrayed the situation in his DealBook interview last week. Nevertheless, one also could argue that the US government, not the vendor, controls the use of contractually obligated resources. Be that as it may, Musk raised the bar considerably in October, when he — or Trump — or both — once again dialed down satellite service in Ukraine, exposing that country to further attacks.

It has been revealed that musk attempted to mollify bipartisan outrage over the debacle with yet another publicity stunt for SpaceX. However, service interruptions have continued into this week. Meanwhile, Trump has spent the same week cozying up to both Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, aided and abetted by an obedient Republican majority in Congress.

It has been revealed that that majority will evaporate, though, in January 3, which is just around the corner. The incoming Democratic majority is already gearing up for a fight. In a letter dated November 20, the incoming Chair of the House Intelligence Committee, Jim Himes (D-CT), demanded an in-person briefing from senior SpaceX officers, seeking an explanation for the disruption of military-grade Starshield service in Ukraine. As leverage, Himes warned Musk that a Democratic majority in Congress will do what the Republican majority failed to do, namely, exercise its constitutional authority over federal contracts.

Referring specifically to SpaceX’s military-grade Starshield satellite services in Ukraine, Himes warned Musk that his entire suite of present and future SpaceX security contracts with the US government is at risk. “SpaceX’s potentially unilateral modification of a U.S. Government contract, combined with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight, calls into question every contract the U.S. Government has with SpaceX,” Himes explained.

“For that reason, it is difficult for me to continue supporting the authorization of funding for these SpaceX- developed, government-owned systems until I receive satisfactory answers to my questions about the Starshield service in Ukraine,” Himes continued.

In a recent development, will Musk simply ignore the request for a briefing? After all, as Himes notes, Musk failed to respond to earlier requests. Stay tuned….

#64983. Why Do Empty-Nest Boomers Own So Many Homes in Top School Districts?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (977 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Realtor ↗ Open Full Page

Why Do Empty-Nest Boomers Own So Many Homes in Top School Districts?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the best-performing school districts often bring stiff competition from families looking to break in, while older neighbors stay put.
  • The paper from the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland studied the household characteristics of the best-performing school districts in the country, which command higher real estate prices but also a higher barrier to entry.
  • It has been revealed that the Cleveland Fed's findings show that seniors occupy a larger share of households in good school districts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the best-performing school districts often bring stiff competition from families looking to break in, while older neighbors stay put. But helping free up housing in these districts isn't as simple as getting older people to move, a fresh study argues.

The paper from the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland studied the household characteristics of the best-performing school districts in the country, which command higher real estate prices but also a higher barrier to entry.

It has been revealed that the Cleveland Fed's findings show that seniors occupy a larger share of households in good school districts. But it pinned that on affordability challenges. Higher-income households of all types compete for housing in the best-performing school districts.

Industry observers note that this is a conundrum for neighborhoods. Seniors are thus left in neighborhoods paying premiums for school districts they don't use. Meanwhile young families who'd like move into the district face limited options for homes there.

In a recent development, of course, many seniors want to age in place in homes that they've lived in for decades. But others looking to downsize are "locked in" due to high mortgage rates. That can leave them in homes that they can't afford or, worse, in homes that pose safety risks for aging people.

"These findings suggest that policies aimed solely at encouraging older households to downsize are unlikely to substantially improve access to quality school districts," the paper says.

Low housing turnover in these districts drives up prices. The higher-rated public school districts are, on average, 49% more expensive, and homes there move faster, Realtor.com® data reveals. But in some of the nation's top school districts—including in Dallas, Los Angeles, and San Fransisco—homes can sell for three times the price of surrounding metros.

Using data from the American Community Survey, the Cleveland Fed found that households over 65 occupy a disproportionate share of the housing stock in the best-performing school districts. While these account for 26.2% of all households nationally, they make up as much as 28.7% of households in the least affordable areas.

Meanwhile households with children, which make up about 31.2% of U.S. households, occupy 30.1% of housing in the best school districts and 40% of the housing stock in the lowest-quality districts. The same doesn't ring true for one-person households, which tend to be more evenly distributed.

Older homeowners move at about the same rate across all school districts—about 6.9% a year. About 81% of older adults in the best school districts own their homes. To the Cleveland Fed, that reveals older households aren't limiting turnover of housing stock in high-quality and high-cost districts.

"While older households occupy a modestly larger share of housing in these expensive, high-quality areas, they do not appear to limit turnover," the paper states. "These patterns suggest that the challenge of accessing high-quality school districts is driven by a combination of income sorting and competition from multiple household types rather than solely by empty-nesters’ aging in place.".

Industry observers note that realtor.com senior economist Jiayi Xu says a few challenges are affecting seniors as they consider their futures. They include capital gains taxes they'd incur on homes that have appreciated in value. They also include the kinds of taxes they'd incur when they move to a upcoming place. Then there are the social considerations.

Recent findings suggest that "Right-sized, single-level, accessible homes near family and doctors are scarce," Xu says. "Moving also means leaving behind the neighbors and community that owners have built over decades. For many longtime owners, there are few good places to go.".

In a recent development, buyers can still find deals in some of these good markets, Realtor.com found, if they look carefully. But in some good districts, there simply aren't a lot of homes changing hands.

It has been revealed that xu adds that she's surprised that young professionals without children can also compete for housing in these expensive districts. Jobs, urban amenities, and investment opportunity for the real estate tend to make these areas attractive.

Recent findings suggest that "Even if more seniors moved, the homes they left would likely go to higher-income buyers, because this is a sorting story. The districts wouldn’t become much more affordable," Xu states. "The more direct solution is building more homes in and near high-demand districts. Adding right-sized options could also give older owners who want to move somewhere to go, but supply is what would ease pressure on prices.".

It has been revealed that to Arick Morton, CEO of NIC MAP, the frozen market points to a need for more housing oriented toward seniors. Earlier this year, his group said the nation needs to add 1 million new senior housing units by 2040. That $1 trillion homebuilding frenzy would meet the moment 10 million baby boomers pass age 80.

Recent findings suggest that "People stay at home much longer than they did previously," Morton said. "Of course folks stay at home as long as they can and then movie into senior housing when the need is there.".

But when there isn't enough senior housing or they don't have good alternatives to downsize, those seniors end up displaced when age or an accident means they require more intensive care needs.

Industry observers note that "The best policy options are those that help expedite the construction of senior housing," Morton remarked. "We don't have enough capacity to create a dent in that logjam.".

Tristan Navera is a senior reporter on housing policy, covering trends and solutions in the housing market from Washington, DC. He was previously a senior reporter at Bloomberg Law, and before that covered real estate for the Washington Business Journal. Earlier in his career, he spent a decade reporting on business and real estate in Dayton and Columbus, OH. A Cincinnati native, he holds a journalism degree from Ohio University.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Your favorite same-day-delivery online superstore wants to give you gas. That's right: Amazon, the one-stop shop for furniture, groceries, health care, and household knickknacks, is now offering its Prime members an additional fuel-saving perk. Already in a fuel-savings friendship with energy tech giant BP, Amazon is now doubling its daily discount to 20 cents off per gallon. But, of course, there's some fine print attached. The significant bonus is exclusive to Amazon Prime members with active earnify account, only applies to one fill up every Friday, and lasts through January 2027.

Industry observers note that the marketplace that Jeff Bezos built learned its lesson with standalone convenience stores, so instead of building gas stations or buying up existing chains, Amazon is letting BP handle the brick-and-mortar thing. BP's earnify rewards app was introduced in 2024 and now offers discounts at the pump and inside convenience stores.

The standard fuel discount for all earnify members is 5 cents off a gallon, but its partnership with Amazon, which started the same year earnify debuted, allows Amazon Prime members to enjoy an everyday deal of 10 cents off per gallon every day and 20 cents on Fuel Up Fridays.

This isn't the first time Amazon has helped improve motorists' weekend vibes either. The last Fuel Up Fridays promo happened earlier this year and lasted from April 3 to May 29, and before that, the special ran from October 17 until December 26, 2025. Blame (or thank) the economy, but the current savings spree is going to last more than three months. Since October 2, Fuel Up Fridays has been up and running. If you're doing any winter holiday travels by RV, car, or truck, you're in luck because the Amazon-BP discount continues beyond the Fresh Year. Although you can't always avoid dumb winter drivers, at least you know you can save 20 cents during fill-ups until January 29.

It has been revealed that you don't have to only stick with BP-branded gas stations for this special promotion, either. It applies to all BP and Amoco locations, as well as participating ampm and Thorntons stores. That means you have more than 7,500 pit stops across the U.S. to choose from.

For the Amazon fuel deal, the sign-up process requires a one-time activation. Prime members can claim the gas discount via the Amazon Fuel page on a web browser or by scrolling through the Partner Offers section under the Prime category in the app. A caveat of the TGIF 20-cents-off bonus is that it can only be used only on one fill-up every Friday, and maxes out at 35 gallons. And given how BP is making a fortune drilling oil, giving back 10 cents on the gallon is the very least they can do.
